problems.title: Count integers between two logarithms
problems.question: How many natural numbers lie in [log₂7,log₃100]?
problems.idea: Bound the logarithms between small integers.
steps: The lower endpoint is between 2 and 3, and the upper endpoint between 4 and 5.
The only integers in the interval are 3 and 4.
There are two.

problems.title: A logarithm with a powered base
problems.question: Find log_(b²)(a⁵b⁴) if logₐb=5.
problems.idea: Change to base b and divide by the power in the base.
steps: The given equality implies log_b a=1/5.
Then log_b(a⁵b⁴)=5·(1/5)+4=5.
Divide by 2: the answer is 5/2.

problems.title: Infinitely many intersections with an oscillating sine
problems.question: How many real solutions does (1/3)ˣ-3sin3x=0 have?
problems.idea: On every sufficiently far-right positive sine hump, the difference changes sign on each side of the peak.
formulas: Sine is continuous, has infinitely many positive humps, and reaches 1 on each.
(1/3)ˣ is positive and tends to 0 as x→∞.
A continuous sign change guarantees a root.
steps: At either endpoint of a positive sine hump, sin3x=0, so the difference is positive.
At a far-right peak, sin3x=1 and (1/3)ˣ<3, so the difference is negative.
There is a zero between the left endpoint and peak, and another between the peak and right endpoint.
Infinitely many disjoint humps give infinitely many roots.

problems.title: Rationalise a radical limit
problems.question: Find lim as n→1 of (√(n+3)-2)/(n-1).
problems.idea: Multiply by the conjugate before taking the limit.
steps: For n≠1, multiply numerator and denominator by √(n+3)+2.
The numerator becomes n+3-4=n-1, which cancels.
The remaining expression is 1/(√(n+3)+2), whose limit is 1/4.

problems.title: Read a nested radical before cancelling logarithms
problems.question: Simplify $8^{\frac23\log_2\sqrt{3+\sqrt2}}\,27^{\frac13\log_3(3-\sqrt2)}$.
problems.idea: Use bases 8=2³ and 27=3³.
steps: The first factor is 2^(2log₂√(3+√2))=(√(3+√2))²=3+√2.
The second is 3^(log₃(3-√2))=3-√2.
Multiply the conjugates to get 7. Both logarithm arguments are positive.
problems.note: The outer radical in the first exponent covers 3+√2. It is not the sum √3+√2.

problems.title: A logarithm of a reciprocal radical
problems.question: Evaluate log_(√a-√(a-1))(√a+√(a-1)) for a>2.
problems.idea: The two conjugate quantities multiply to one.
steps: Put b=√a-√(a-1). It is positive and less than 1, so it is a valid base.
The argument is 1/b.
Therefore its logarithm to base b is -1.

problems.title: Minimum of a line with a logarithmic slope
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=xlog₄(√2-1) on [-1,1].
problems.idea: The constant slope is negative.
steps: A linear function with negative slope decreases as x increases.
Its minimum on the closed interval occurs at x=1.
The minimum value is log₄(√2-1).

problems.title: A cone from a perpendicular to a generator midpoint
problems.question: The perpendicular from a cone’s base centre to a generator has length 3√2 and bisects that generator. Find the volume.
problems.idea: The right axial half-triangle has equal legs because the centre is on the generator’s perpendicular bisector.
formulas: In an isosceles right triangle with leg r, the altitude to the hypotenuse is r/√2.
steps: Let O be the base centre, S the apex and A the base point of the generator.
The perpendicular-bisector condition gives OS=OA, hence h=r.
The altitude r/√2 equals 3√2, so r=h=6.
The volume is π·36·6/3=72π.

problems.title: Cone volume from an equilateral axial section
problems.question: A cone’s axial section is equilateral with area 4√3. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Its base is the diameter and its altitude is the cone height.
steps: From s²√3/4=4√3, obtain s=4.
The cone radius is r=s/2=2 and height h=2√3.
The volume is π·4·2√3/3=8π√3/3.

problems.title: Remove two cones from a cylinder
problems.question: Two cones are removed from a cylinder. Both have apex at the cylinder axis midpoint and each has one cylinder base as its base. Find remaining volume divided by original volume.
problems.idea: Each cone has the cylinder radius and half its height.
formulas: Cylinder volume πr²H; cone volume πr²h/3.
steps: Each removed cone has volume πr²(H/2)/3=πr²H/6.
Together they remove one-third of the cylinder volume.
The remaining fraction is 1-1/3=2/3.

problems.title: Perpendicular generators and a base-circle arc ratio
problems.question: Two perpendicular generators of a cone divide the base circumference in ratio 1:2. The cone height is 2√2. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The shorter arc has central angle 120°. Use the dot product of the two generator vectors.
steps: Perpendicularity gives h²-r²/2=0, so r²=2h².
The given height has h²=8, hence r²=16.
The volume is π·16·2√2/3=32π√2/3.

problems.title: Radius ratio of equal-volume cone and cylinder
problems.question: A cone and cylinder have equal volumes and equal heights. Find cone radius divided by cylinder radius.
problems.idea: Equate their volume formulas and cancel the height.
formulas: Cone volume πR²h/3; cylinder volume πr²h.
steps: Equality gives R²/3=r².
Radii are positive, so R=√3r.
The requested ratio R/r is √3.

problems.title: Count pyramid vertices from edges and faces
problems.question: A pyramid has 7 more edges than faces. Find its number of vertices.
problems.idea: Use an n-sided base to count all three quantities.
formulas: Edges E=2n, faces F=n+1, vertices V=n+1.
steps: The condition is 2n-(n+1)=7.
Thus n=8.
The eight base vertices and apex give 9 vertices.

problems.title: Lateral area from rhombus diagonal sections
problems.question: A right prism has rhombus base and diagonal-section areas 6,8. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: The rhombus diagonals bisect at right angles, allowing the side length times height to be recovered.
formulas: For diagonals p,q, rhombus side s=√(p²+q²)/2.
Diagonal-section areas are ph,qh; lateral area=4sh.
steps: We know ph=6 and qh=8.
The lateral area is 4sh=20.

problems.title: Conjugate bases in a power inequality
problems.question: Solve $((\sqrt5-1)/2)^x>((\sqrt5+1)/2)^3$.
problems.idea: The two positive bases are reciprocals.
steps: Let A=(√5-1)/2, so 0<A<1 and the other base equals A⁻¹.
The inequality becomes Aˣ>A⁻³.
Because the exponential is decreasing, x<-3.

problems.title: A telescoping logarithm product
problems.question: Evaluate log₃5·log₅7·log₇9.
problems.idea: Change all factors to the same logarithm base.
steps: The intermediate ln5 and ln7 factors cancel.
The product becomes ln9/ln3=log₃9.
Because 9=3², it equals 2.

problems.title: An exponential equation with logarithms on both sides
problems.question: Solve $x^{\log_3 19}=19^{\log_3(2x-16)}$.
problems.idea: Use the symmetry u^(log_b v)=v^(log_b u).
formulas: For positive u,v and valid base b, u^(log_b v)=v^(log_b u).
steps: The logarithm requires 2x-16>0, hence x>8; this also makes x positive.
Rewrite the left side as 19^(log₃x).
The base 19 is one-to-one, so log₃x=log₃(2x-16), giving x=2x-16.
Thus x=16, which satisfies the domain.

problems.title: Domain of a logarithm with a variable base
problems.question: Find the domain of y=log_(2x-x²)(16-x²).
problems.idea: Both argument and base must be positive, and the base cannot equal one.
steps: 16-x²>0 gives -4<x<4.
2x-x²=x(2-x)>0 gives 0<x<2.
The base equals 1 when 2x-x²=1, or (x-1)²=0, so exclude x=1.
Intersecting the conditions leaves (0,1)∪(1,2).

problems.title: A limit of two square roots
problems.question: Find lim as n→∞ of [√(n²+2n+5)+√(n²-2n+5)]/(2n+1).
problems.idea: Divide numerator and denominator by positive n.
formulas: 1/n and 1/n² tend to zero as n→∞.
steps: The quotient becomes [√(1+2/n+5/n²)+√(1-2/n+5/n²)]/(2+1/n).
Each square root tends to 1 and the denominator tends to 2.
The limit is (1+1)/2=1.

problems.title: Frustum volume from an axial diagonal
problems.question: A conical frustum’s axial-section diagonals divide each other in ratio 2:1. A diagonal has length 3 m and makes 30° with the base. Find the frustum volume.
problems.idea: The axial section is an isosceles trapezoid whose base ratio equals the diagonal-division ratio.
formulas: Height h=d sinθ; horizontal diagonal projection=R+r=d cosθ.
steps: The larger-to-smaller radius ratio is R:r=2:1.
The height is 3sin30°=3/2 and R+r=3√3/2.
Thus r=√3/2 and R=√3.
The squared-radius combination is 3+3/2+3/4=21/4.
The volume is π(3/2)(21/4)/3=21π/8 m³.

problems.title: Two logarithms that are both negative
problems.question: Solve log₃(x-4)+log₄(5-x)<0.
problems.idea: The domain makes both arguments lie strictly between zero and one.
formulas: For base b>1 and 0<t<1, log_b t<0.
steps: The domain requires x>4 and x<5.
For 4<x<5, both x-4 and 5-x lie in (0,1).
Both logarithms are strictly negative, so their sum is negative throughout the domain.

problems.title: Cylinder radius from two perpendicular vertical cuts
problems.question: Two cylinder sections share one generator and make a right angle. The axis-to-plane distances are 2.5 and 6. The height is 4. Find the volume.
problems.idea: In a horizontal cross-section, the two planes become perpendicular lines meeting on the base circle.
formulas: For perpendicular lines through a point P, distance(OP)² equals the sum of squared distances from O to the lines.
steps: The shared generator meets the base circle at P. Its distance from the axis point O is the radius r.
Because the section lines are perpendicular, r²=2.5²+6²=6.25+36=169/4.
The volume is π·(169/4)·4=169π.

problems.title: Ratio of geometric-series limits
problems.question: Find the limit as n→∞ of (1/2+1/4+...+1/2ⁿ)/(1/3+1/9+...+1/3ⁿ).
problems.idea: Evaluate the two convergent geometric sums.
steps: The numerator tends to (1/2)/(1-1/2)=1.
The denominator tends to (1/3)/(1-1/3)=1/2.
The denominator limit is nonzero, so the quotient tends to 1/(1/2)=2.

problems.title: Volume of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: All six edges of a triangular pyramid are 6. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The apex lies above the equilateral base centre.
steps: With a=6, the base area is 9√3 and the height is 2√6.
Simplify to 18√2.

problems.title: A parameter and two potentially coincident roots
problems.question: For which a does (4x+a)log₄(x-4)=0 have exactly one real solution?
problems.idea: Count roots only in x>4, and remember that the two factors may give the same root.
steps: The logarithm domain is x>4. Its own zero always gives x=5.
The linear root lies in the domain exactly when -a/4>4, or a<-16.
For a≥-16, only x=5 remains.
For a<-16 there are normally two roots, except when -a/4=5, namely a=-20. Then both roots coincide.
problems.note: None of the listed intervals includes exactly this set; the isolated coincidence a=-20 is essential.
